prompt: The website leaves `discount` blank where the app writes `0`. What do the website's blanks mean?
hint: Compare which coupons appear in each channel.

choices.text: A coupon the website failed to save to the order record
choices.why: Lost coupons would leave the coupon values rarer on the website; they occur at the same rate as in the app.

choices.text: No coupon: a discount of zero, written as a blank
choices.why: Right. The coupons appear as values in both channels; the blank is the website's spelling of none.

choices.text: The customer declined to say whether they had a coupon
choices.why: A coupon is applied by the checkout, not declared by the customer.

choices.text: A discount still being calculated at export time
choices.why: Nothing in the orders is pending; these are orders from the whole year.

prompt: Which of these values stand for an absence rather than measure something? Choose all that apply.
hint: Ask what each value records about the world.

choices.text: A birth year of `1900`
choices.why: Yes. It is the form's placeholder for a year nobody gave.

choices.text: A blank `nps` on the survey
choices.why: Yes. The customer did not answer.

choices.text: A `0` discount written by the app
choices.why: No. Zero is the real discount on an order without a coupon.

choices.text: A delivery time of `119` minutes
choices.why: No. It is a real, slow delivery, the longest the timer recorded.

prompt: A value typed only because a form demanded one, such as `1900` in `birth_year`, is a ___.
hint: It holds the place of a value.

prompt: Match each cause of a blank to its kind.
hint: Does the blank depend on nothing, on a visible column, on the value itself, or is there no value to have?

pairs.left: A cable fault drops one reading in a hundred
The timer stops at two hours
A pickup has no delivery time

prompt: Which kind of blank is the only one the data alone cannot reveal?
hint: Its cause is the thing that is missing.

choices.text: MCAR
choices.why: MCAR leaves a trace: rows with and without a value look alike.

choices.text: MAR
choices.why: MAR shows up as blanks lining up with a visible column.

choices.text: MNAR
choices.why: Right. MNAR looks like MAR from inside the file; the clue has to come from outside.

choices.text: Not applicable
choices.why: That one is the easiest: a value could not exist, and another column says so.

prompt: If a column's blanks are MCAR, what is true of an average over the rows that have a value?
hint: The rows with a value are a fair sample of all the rows.

choices.text: Unbiased, but less precise
choices.why: Right. Fewer rows, same target.

choices.text: Biased downwards, because the blanks were the larger values
choices.why: That would be MNAR, the timer's case.

choices.text: Biased in a direction a visible column predicts
choices.why: That describes MAR, where groups differ.

choices.text: Impossible to compute until the blanks are filled in
choices.why: An average over the present rows is computed every day; the question is whether it is fair.

prompt: At a clinic, weight is blank for every patient who refused to step on the scale, and the people who refuse are heavier on average. What kind of blank is this?
hint: What does the decision to refuse depend on?

choices.text: MAR: the refusal is recorded in its own column
choices.why: Recording that somebody refused does not record what they weigh.

choices.text: MCAR: patients refuse for their own reasons
choices.why: Their reasons are tied to the value, which is the opposite of MCAR.

choices.text: Not applicable: no weight was taken
choices.why: Every patient has a weight; it was not measured.

choices.text: MNAR: the refusal depends on the weight itself
choices.why: Right. The missing values are systematically higher than the recorded ones.

prompt: What is the right treatment for the blank `delivery_minutes` of a pickup?
hint: No delivery took place.

choices.text: Fill it with zero minutes, since nothing was delivered at all
choices.why: A zero would pull every average of delivery time down with deliveries that never happened.

choices.text: Fill it with the average delivery time of that same day
choices.why: That invents a delivery for an order that was collected.

choices.text: Leave it blank; test deliveries only
choices.why: Right. The blank is correct, and completeness should be measured over deliveries.

choices.text: Drop the pickups
choices.why: They are real orders with real revenue; only the delivery fields do not apply.

prompt: 15,406 of the 23,594 store sales have no customer. What percentage is that? Give one decimal place.
Sales with a loyalty number average R$ 65.58 and sales without one average R$ 65.68. What does that show?
hint: A failed search for a difference is not proof of sameness.

choices.text: Proof that the identified customers represent everyone
choices.why: One matching average proves nothing about frequency, products or anything else.

choices.text: No evidence that the two groups buy differently
choices.why: Right. The most obvious difference is absent, which is not proof that every other one is.

choices.text: That the blanks must be filled before revenue is reported
choices.why: Revenue does not need the customer at all.

choices.text: That walk-in customers spend ten centavos more each
choices.why: A ten-centavo difference between two averages of thousands of sales is noise, not a finding.

prompt: A cell of the missingness map reads 100%. What does that say about that column in that group?
hint: All or nothing in a group is an explanation.

choices.text: The column is useless and should be dropped
choices.why: The same column is 93% filled in other groups.

choices.text: The blanks are random within the group
choices.why: At 100% there is nothing random left: every row is blank.

choices.text: The export failed for that group
choices.why: The other columns of the same rows are filled.

choices.text: The group fully explains the blanks, so they need no further search
choices.why: Right, as with every pickup's courier and every Rapidex time.

prompt: Why are the 643 cancelled own-fleet orders set aside before studying the blank times?
hint: What would there have been to time?

choices.text: Nothing was delivered, so nothing to time
choices.why: Right. Their blanks are not applicable, like the pickups'.

choices.text: Cancelled orders are not part of 2025's data
choices.why: They are in the 2025 file; they simply had no delivery.

choices.text: Their times were deleted when they were cancelled
choices.why: There was never a time to delete.

choices.text: They belong to Rapidex
choices.why: These are own-fleet orders by definition.

prompt: 456 own-fleet deliveries have no time and 14,858 have one. What percentage of the 15,314 lacks a time? Give one decimal place.
The longest recorded delivery is 119 minutes, and 309 deliveries fall between 110 and 119. Which observation is the strongest clue that the blanks are MNAR?
hint: What should the end of a long tail look like?

choices.text: The tail is still thick one band before it stops at a round number
choices.why: Right. A tail that thins out does not end at 119 with 309 deliveries in its last band.

choices.text: The median is 56 minutes
choices.why: The middle of the distribution is ordinary; it says nothing about the blanks.

choices.text: Evening deliveries are blank four times as often
choices.why: That fits MAR on the hour just as well; it cannot tell the two apart.

choices.text: Only 3% of deliveries have no time
choices.why: A small rate says nothing about the mechanism.

prompt: Blanks are four times as common between 18:00 and 21:00. Why is "MAR on the hour" the wrong conclusion here?
hint: What do evening deliveries have more of?

choices.text: Couriers stop working at 21:00, so the timer is switched off early
choices.why: Nothing in the files or from operations says so.

choices.text: The website's evening orders are stored in UTC and look like night
choices.why: The split used only the app's orders, whose times are local.

choices.text: Evenings are slower
choices.why: Right. The hour predicts long deliveries, and the length is what empties the field.

choices.text: Too few evening deliveries exist to measure a rate
choices.why: Evenings are the busiest hours of the day.

prompt: Late deliveries were 10.5% of the recorded times and 13.2% of the real ones. How many percentage points did the blanks hide?
hint: Subtract.

prompt: Who could confirm that the own-fleet blanks are deliveries of two hours or more?
hint: The source knows what the data cannot say.

choices.text: Another analyst reading the same file
choices.why: Another reading of the file finds the same ambiguity.

choices.text: The operations team, which runs the app
choices.why: Right. They know the couriers' app and its two-hour limit.

choices.text: A statistical test on the recorded times
choices.why: A test on what was recorded cannot see what was not.

choices.text: The customers who placed those orders
choices.why: They know their delivery was slow, not why the field is empty.

prompt: Put the steps Ana took with the own-fleet blanks in order.
hint: Remove what is explained before chasing what is not.
items: Set aside pickups, Rapidex and cancelled orders
Split the remaining blanks by the hour
Notice the recorded times stop at 119
Ask operations how the timer works
Write the mechanism in the missingness log
trap: Asking before looking wastes the source's time; writing before asking records a guess as a fact.

prompt: The NPS from the answers is 40.6 and the NPS of everybody invited is 31.3. Why is the first one higher?
hint: Who skips a survey?

choices.text: The survey is only sent to customers who received their order on time
choices.why: It goes to every delivered online order, slow ones included.

choices.text: Scores of 7 and 8 are left out of the calculation by mistake
choices.why: Leaving out 7 and 8 is how NPS is defined: they are neither promoters nor detractors.

choices.text: The truth file uses a different scale from the survey
choices.why: Both are scores from 0 to 10.

choices.text: Unhappy customers answer less
choices.why: Right. The answers over-represent the satisfied, so the score is flattered.

prompt: In a month, 50% of the answers are 9 or 10 and 15% are 6 or less. What is the NPS?
hint: Promoters minus detractors.

prompt: Which of these belong in a careful report of the NPS? Choose all that apply.
hint: Nothing recovers the missing scores.

choices.text: The response rate beside the score
choices.why: Yes. The reader needs it to weigh the number.

choices.text: A comparison of respondents and non-respondents on what is known about both
choices.why: Yes, as the delivery-time bands did.

choices.text: The blanks filled with the average answer
choices.why: That repeats the bias with more confidence: the average answer is the flattered one.

choices.text: The trend from month to month
choices.why: Yes. A stable selection leaves a falling trend meaningful.

choices.text: Only the months with a response rate above 50%
choices.why: No month comes near it, and choosing months by rate is another selection.

prompt: Delivery time predicts who answers the survey, yet the lesson calls the blanks MNAR. Why?
hint: Think of bruised mangoes.

choices.text: Delivery time is itself missing for every survey
choices.why: It is present for every own-fleet delivery the survey covers.

choices.text: Satisfaction drives both the score and the decision to give it
choices.why: Right. Delivery time is only a visible shadow of the missing value.

choices.text: The survey was sent at random to a sample of orders
choices.why: It goes to every delivered online order, not a sample.

choices.text: Scores from 0 to 10 cannot be MAR
choices.why: The scale has nothing to do with the mechanism.

prompt: Put the five questions for a column with blanks in the order the lesson asks them.
hint: Start with whether a value should exist at all.
items: Could a value exist here at all?
What does the source system mean by a blank?
Do the blanks line up with a visible column?
Is there a sign the value itself is involved?
trap: Testing for a hidden value before ruling out the visible explanations sends you looking for a ceiling in a column of pickups.

prompt: What makes the `confirmed by` column of the missingness log worth keeping?
hint: A mechanism nobody confirmed is a hypothesis.

choices.text: It separates evidence from belief, and names who to ask
choices.why: Right, and it names who to ask again when a system changes.

choices.text: It lets the log be sorted by team when the data is handed over
choices.why: Sorting is not the point; knowing what is known is.

choices.text: Auditors require a name beside every column of every data set
choices.why: No such rule is cited; the column exists for the next reader.

choices.text: It records who filled in the blanks
choices.why: Nothing has been filled yet; that is lesson 4.

prompt: A formal test on the data rejects MCAR for a column. What has it established?
hint: The data can rule mechanisms out, not in.

choices.text: That the blanks are MNAR
choices.why: Rejecting MCAR leaves both MAR and MNAR standing.

choices.text: That the blanks are MAR
choices.why: MNAR passes the same test in the same way.

choices.text: That the blanks are not completely random, and nothing about MAR against MNAR
choices.why: Right. Telling MAR from MNAR needs something the file does not hold.

choices.text: That the column has to be dropped
choices.why: A test describes the blanks; what to do is lesson 4's decision.

prompt: In a loan file, income is blank for most self-employed applicants and present for employees, and `employment_type` is in the file. Within each type, nothing else predicts a blank. What kind is it?
hint: The blanks depend on a column you can see, and on nothing else.

choices.text: MCAR, because nothing else predicts a blank within a type
choices.why: Across types the rate differs sharply, so it is not completely random.

choices.text: MNAR, because self-employed incomes vary more than salaries
choices.why: Variation is not the cause of the blank; the employment type is.

choices.text: Not applicable, since self-employed people have no salary
choices.why: They have an income, which is what the column asks for.

choices.text: MAR, explained by the `employment_type` column in the file
choices.why: Right. Within each type the blanks are random, so fixes work group by group.

prompt: Match each blank to what it means.
hint: The missingness log has the answers.
